summary:
FINAL CREATIVE PLAN, round 1, finalized after the second critic pass (media buyer, compliance, scent/evidence). The campaign is cold, top of funnel, for a brand nobody knows. Avatar, awareness, angles and funnel are unchanged: the Pad-and-Liner Mom, problem-aware, moment-first. Angles are A1 the moment / A2 not a pad, not a diaper / A3 it's just underwear. Every ad hands off to the one live hero ('Stop! I'll pee myself! / Common? Yes. Normal? No. / Find your match.') with a=m and utm_content=moment/pads/underwear.

VIDEOS (9, all made with AI):
- V1 (A2), liner in hand plus brand VO over b-roll. Ranked proof: Everdries 1206351388295667 at 275d (video#14). That is the only proof for the impersonal-narrator opener; UltraDries 896552676720439 and 1730018818434803 prove the visuals only.
- V2 (A3), AI 3D talking duet: a Pixar-style panty liner and a plain black brief. The best-proven AI format in the category: 6 talking-object creatives live 104-208d, ranked #4/#11/#11. One of them (1691171645641479, 180d) is our exact cast.
- V3 (A1), silent on-body clip with one moment line. It's the only format whose first frame is the landing H1, word for word.

STATICS (6):
- S1 (A2), native liner phone photo with a long story caption (UltraDries image#1/#3 at 202-209d, Carol image#6 at 152d).
- S4 (A1), text-led cards (Carol image#1 listicle at 249d; the one-line cards are a Tier B test).

VISUAL HOOKS (Miro board, all re-verified against the export). Each format tests 3 different hooks:
- V1: 75 handbag POV / 42 freeze-frame / 33 camera wipe (NEW, replaces the 34 trash match cut)
- V2: 117 opened three ways: +70 lean-in / +38 in media res / +04 A vs B
- V3: 72+33 stop-hand wipe / 62 reenactment / 52+70 move-in-frame stare (NEW, staged like the Revival twin; 12 is the backup)
- S1: 135 / 06 / 55 holding prop (NEW, replaces 51)
- S4: 09 / 12 / 22

TOP HOOKS (score 9):
- V3-a: a palm thrown at the lens wipes into 'Stop! I'll pee myself!' at 0.3s.
- V2-a: the liner's confession, now naming the leak in its first words: 'I'm the liner she wears for the sneeze-pee. And I need to be honest.'

Score 8-8.5: V1-b (wide dinner two-shot with the H1 burned in at 0.1s, then a freeze), V2-b (now laugh-led: off-screen 'Stop! I'll pee myself!' and the liner leaps out of the clutch), V1-a (post-sneeze grab with the proven contrarian line on screen from 0.5s), V1-c (liner wiped across the lens into the brief), V2-c, V3-b, V3-c, S1-b, S4-a, S4-b.

Lowest: S1-a, S1-c and S4-c at 7.5. There's nothing under 7.5 now.

This round's hard fixes:
- No AI woman repeats the trigger after the brief appears, so there's no acted performance demo.
- 'Dramatization' moves to the upper-left safe zone.
- Licensed audio only.
- A buildable voice pipeline for the talking characters.
- Product frames come from the sample photos only (NUMBER_SHEET §13 still lists the old lace product).
- The Advanced Health line is re-cited honestly as a Tier B caption line.

Gates before ANY spend:
1. Fake reviews off the landing.
2. Pixel with health params stripped.
3. Guarantee terms, L0-L3 and the AI line live.
4. Founder wear test logged for a sneeze AND a big laugh. This gates every ad; the jump gates V3-c only.
5. Size range measured.
6. Hero copy frozen.
7. 5 reference photos of the real sample taken.

video_formats.format: Problem object + brand voiceover over b-roll. A clean liner is the hook, the plain black brief is the payoff, and an impersonal brand narrator carries the VO.
video_formats.why_this_format:
About 8 Tier A voiceover ads open on a pad or diaper (of 137 classified Tier A ads). It carries the most-proven problem/solution angle in the set: pads-wrong/replace-pads = 44 Tier A ads.

What each reference proves:
- The impersonal brand-narrator opener, plus the contrarian on-screen question over the problem object: Everdries 1206351388295667 ONLY (275d, video#14, 'It's 2025! Why are you still using pads?').
- The pad-in-hand wave: UltraDries 896552676720439 (193d, video#6). Its VO is first-person UGC until 13.9s.
- Hands-only flat-lay b-roll: Everdries 1730018818434803 (124d). Its VO is also first person.
Those two prove the visuals, not the voice.

Honest caveat: VO places only 2 of 29 in a top-10. So every V1 hook now opens on a pattern interrupt with the hook line burned in on screen:
- V1-a: handbag-cam POV
- V1-b: freeze-frame
- V1-c: camera wipe
The brand appears late, which suits cold traffic.
video_formats.structure:
Two cuts: about 35s and about 55s.
- 0-3s, hook: the Miro visual hook. The moment or the liner is in frame 1, and the word sneeze/pee/laugh is ON SCREEN by 1s. The hook line is burned in, never VO-only.
- 3-18s: brand VO over liner b-roll, CJ attributes only. 'It bunches. It shifts. It feels like a diaper. And by tonight it's in the trash.'
- 18-32s: reveal the plain black brief.
  - Real-sample-based shot stretched in hand.
  - Then an AI woman, side-on, waist-to-knee or full figure, pulling black leggings up over it.
  - Then ONE everyday movement in leggings: walk, bend or reach. Never a laugh, sneeze or jump.
- 32-40s: 'Not a pad, not a diaper.' Add 'For the sneeze, the laugh and the jump' only if the logged wear test covers the jump. If it logs the sneeze and laugh but not the jump, the line stays 'Not a pad, not a diaper.'
- 40-45s, end card: '30 nights to see if they hold.' / 'Find my match'.

No price, gifts, 'new', stats, mechanism or reviews.

Then the offer's pads vs Leapproof table ('go in the trash every day'). V1-b also lands on H1 line 1 'Stop! I'll pee myself!' and the subhead '...rather laugh than cross their legs'. Tags: a=m, utm_content=pads. Ad names are codes only (e.g. V1-a_75_handbag).
video_formats.ai_production:
VO first:
- One impersonal ElevenLabs narrator: a warm, wry woman in her 30s, accent matched to the launch market (NUMBER_SHEET says US-first).
- Record the VO first and cut the pictures to it.
- Never 'I/we' from the narrator, never 'you leak'.

Hooks (Nano Banana start frames, animated 3-4s in Kling 2.x or Veo 3):
- V1-a: handbag-cam interior, already unzipped and lit at frame 0.
- V1-b: one wide restaurant two-shot, then the freeze. No insert cuts in the first 1.2s, which protects face and wardrobe continuity.
- V1-c: one locked hand-held shot at a bathroom vanity. The hand swipes the liner across the lens; on the same framing the hand holds the brief.

V1-c middle beat (trash can): ONE locked AI plate of a white pedal can on cream tiles. Composite cut-out PNGs of crinkled pastel liner WRAPPERS in the edit, adding layers per 'day'. Vary the light with a grade, never a re-generation, so the match cut is pixel-perfect.

Liners: always clean, white and unbranded, or in pastel unbranded wrappers. No stains, no yellow, no real or lookalike brand marks (Always, Carefree, Poise). No car badges.

Payoff:
- Hold every product frame until the 5 reference photos of the real CJ sample (SKU CJNSNYNK00343) exist: flat front, flat back, side, stretched, under leggings.
- Product prompt: 'plain black brief exactly as in the reference photos'. Rise, waistband width, leg line and sheen are copied from the photos, not from text. No lace, no logos, no gusset or seams that aren't on the sample.
- The AI woman is one consistent character (Higgsfield Soul ID / Kling element), 30-45, everyday body.
- Leggings pull-up prompt: 'getting dressed, sports top on, side view, waist-to-knee crop, pulling black leggings up over black briefs'. Generate start and end frames and interpolate 3s.
- Fallback if the models refuse or drift: hands stretching the brief on a bed, then the pull-up framed from the knee to the waistband with the top covering the hip.
- Reject any colour, rise or texture drift.

Text and audio:
- All text added in CapCut/Premiere in the upper safe zone (about 16-60% of frame height, inside the 4:5 centre crop).
- Hanken Grotesk for hook and caption lines; Fraunces for the end-card brand line; brand colours.
- Music only from Meta Sound Collection or a licensed royalty-free library.

Labels:
- 'Dramatization' upper-left (about 16% down) whenever an AI woman is shown in the moment (V1-b only).
- AI disclosure per ai_production_rules.
video_formats.compliance_swaps:
- The only contrast allowed: 'bunches, shifts, feels like a diaper, goes in the trash every day.' Never 'fails', 'leaks through', 'can't hold', 'wrong tool', 'made for periods' or 'built for pee, not blood'.
- 'Why are YOU still using pads?' becomes 'Why is a (panty) liner still the plan for sneeze-pee / a sneeze?' (impersonal).
- No nauseated emoji, no stained pad, no pour/mug demo, no '100%', no absorbency, no layers, no ml.
- No eco words and no $ or volume figures on the trash beat.
- 'Wash. Hang. Wear again.' is the care fact (never 'wash, dry'), as a middle beat only.
- No UTI/rash/chemicals/odour.
- No 'incontinence/discreet/protection/accident/bladder'.
- No sale, no 'original vs new'.
- The AI woman never says anything about the product. Her only line is the dramatized moment (V1-b, labelled).
- After the brief appears she never laughs hard, sneezes or jumps (no acted performance demo).
- No children.

visual_hook.why_for_this_ad:
The camera sits where the product lives (inside the handbag) and the hand comes in to grab it. The viewer sees the ritual from the liner's side: a new point of view in a feed of faces, with the liner (the A2 enemy) dominating frame 1.

The sneeze happens BEFORE the grab, so it's the real post-sneeze spare-liner swap that liner users know, not an impossible pre-sneeze fix.

In-category twin: Everdries 1206351388295667 (275d, video#14), a POV down at the pad with the contrarian question ON SCREEN from frame 1. We copy that by burning the line in at 0.5s.

Why AI makes it better than UGC:
- None of these ads could be shot with UGC.
- No talent, no fake-customer risk, unlimited hook variants.
- A cartoon can say 'pee' and 'sneeze' with humour and zero shame.

What's new about our version: every hook opens on the moment, which no competitor version does:

- Our wry, brand-palette, CJ-safe 35s cut is the untested part.
video_formats.structure:
Two cuts: about 35s (main) and about 60s (long test). Let delivery pick.
- 0-3s, hook: frame 1 is the moment, or a character reacting to it. One character speaks by 0.5s. Burned-in kinetic captions (1-4 words, Hanken Grotesk ExtraBold, cream with a Plum Ink outline, upper-middle safe zone) carry 'pee' or 'sneeze-pee' by 1.2s.

- 12-22s, reveal: the brief answers in brand voice. 'She could just wear underwear. Plain black briefs. Not a pad. Not a diaper.' Cut to a 2-4s real-look insert generated from the CJ sample photos: hands stretching the waistband, then an AI woman, side-on and waist-to-knee, pulling black leggings up over it (getting dressed only). No face on the brief in the inserts.

- 30-35s, end card in brand type: 'Not a pad, not a diaper.' / '30 nights to see if they hold.' / 'Find my match'. Both characters on screen, the liner sulking.

video_formats.ai_production:
Characters:
- Design both in Nano Banana or Midjourney as Pixar-style model sheets: front, 3/4 and 6 expressions.
- The BRIEF is built from the 5 real-sample reference photos: rise, waistband width, leg line and sheen copied from the photos, not from text. No lace (unlike UltraDries' lace-panel brief), no logos. Large friendly eyes and mouth on the upper front panel near the waistband, never at the crotch. Small cream cartoon hands only if needed. Calm, dry, kind.
- The LINER is small, clean, white and unbranded. Expressive, fussy, sheepish (the BFS #4 tone, not Everdries' villain). No stains, no yellowing, no gross-out.
- Don't build the brief model sheet until the reference photos exist.

Sets: real-looking, in brand palette, adult only, no medical props, no real trademarks.
- a cream bathroom shelf with a mirror (V2-a)
- a candle-lit restaurant table with an open black clutch and a wine glass (V2-b)
- a white duvet with a Claret throw and lamp light (V2-c)

Voice pipeline (pick one; test one 8s line both ways before building the 35s):
- Path A (default): generate each line image-to-video in Veo 3 from the locked model-sheet frame, with the dialogue in the prompt (native lip-sync). Then run every line through ElevenLabs Voice Changer (speech-to-speech) into the two saved character voices: Brief = warm, dry, mid-30s; Liner = higher, fussy, fast. Timing and mouth movement are kept, and the voices match across shots.
- Path B: record the ElevenLabs lines first, then animate with a lip-sync model built for cartoon faces (e.g. Hedra Character-3). Use Veo/Kling only for non-speaking reaction shots.
- Generate in 4-8s shots and cut on reactions. Higgsfield is the hub for character consistency.

Humans: off-screen SFX and voices (laughter, 'Stop! I'll pee myself!', the sneeze) are audio only. The only human on screen in a duet is V2-a's out-of-focus mirror reflection (her back, brushing her hair, not in the moment).

Inserts (2-4s): the brief alone (stretch, fold) from the reference photos, and an AI woman getting dressed, side-on, waist-to-knee, pulling leggings over it. Fallback crop if the models refuse or drift: knee to waistband with the top covering the hip. No face on the garment in the inserts, so the viewer sees exactly what ships.

Script guardrails:
- The liner may say only: bunch, shift, feel like a diaper, go in the trash every day, 'I'm a sticker'.
- The brief never says 'leak-proof', 'I hold', 'dry', '100%' or 'built/designed/made for pee', and never claims the opposite of the liner's flaws ('I don't bunch').
- The guarantee lives only on the end card.

Watch:
- Lip-sync drift on non-human mouths: regenerate rather than fix in edit.
- The brief morphing into a boyshort or thong between shots: lock the reference every generation.
- Delivery: 9:16, no watermarks (paid tiers; the Everdries ad carries a Veo mark). Keep the C2PA metadata on export.
video_formats.compliance_swaps:
- The characters talk to each other and about 'her', never stating the viewer's condition. A character addressing the other character ('So you think you can replace me?') is fiction between objects, not a viewer line.
- No 'bladder leaks', 'incontinence' or 'protecting women' (UltraDries' pad line).
- No 'fully leak proof', '100 mLs', snap-in booster, organic/PFAS/bleach/chemicals, plastic backing, smell, UTI or rash (all in the references).
- No 'pads fail / can't hold / leak through / made for periods'. No period-underwear jab.
- No villain gross-out face, no stained pad. Nothing mocks HER: the jokes land on the liner.
- Comparisons are form only (sticks on vs pulls on, sticker vs underwear, trash vs wash). No check marks or X marks, no scoreboard verdict. Label pills are neutral ('sticks on' | 'pulls on').
- The brief never implies it handles the moment ('She's wearing me tonight' is cut). It only states what it is ('She's wearing underwear').
- The brief's face sits on the upper front/waistband, never near the crotch.
- No grandma, 60+ or doctor cues. No children.
- No human is shown leaking, so no 'Dramatization' label is needed. AI disclosure per the rules.

visual_hook_principles:
Board: Nikita's Miro 'Visual Hooks Library', https://miro.com/app/board/uXjVHhmCPn0=/ (131 hooks, 5 categories). Every pick and every miro_example_links URL was re-checked against the board export. Those arrays hold board links only; in-category twins (Ad Library ads) are named in why_for_this_ad and the references.

1) A hook earns its place only if its stopping mechanism IS the moment or the enemy. In frame 1 it must do three things:
- (a) show the moment (laugh, sneeze, the jumping-jacks cue) or the enemy (a clean liner);
- (b) name it ON SCREEN with sneeze/pee/laugh by about 1s, burned in and never VO-only, because most viewers are muted and a stranger mustn't read it as period care;
- (c) set up a line the live hero repeats ('Stop! I'll pee myself!', 'Not a pad, not a diaper', 'Feels like underwear').
Hooks that stop the scroll with something unrelated were dropped. A bait stop sends the wrong click into a 13-question quiz.

2) Hook type follows the angle:
- A1 (the moment) gets body-first hooks: 72+33 Stop-Hand wipe, 62 Problem Reenactment, 52+70 Move In Frame stare, 42 Freeze Frame, 09 Bold Headline, 12 Meme Caption.
- A2 (the enemy) gets object-first hooks: 75 handbag-cam POV, 33 Camera Wipe, 135 Out-of-Place, 06 Red Circle, 55 Holding Prop.
- A3 (just underwear) gets character and comparison hooks: 117 3D Talking Character, opened with 70 Lean-In, 38 In Media Res or 04 A vs B.

- V1 = 75 / 42 / 33
- V2 = 117+70 / 117+38 / 04+117
- V3 = 72+33 / 62 / 52+70
- S1 = 135 / 06 / 55
- S4 = 09 / 12 / 22
Moments are spread so no format is one-note: V2 = sneeze-pee / laugh / face-off; S1 = sneeze / laugh-normal / dinner laugh. Lines repeat across formats on purpose so a winner can be re-cut: 'Stop! I'll pee myself!' in V1-b / V2-b / V3-a / S4-a; the sneeze leg-press in V3-b / S4-b. V1-b (wide two-shot, freeze) and V3-a (close-up, palm wipe) are framed differently so Meta doesn't treat them as near-duplicates.

- The camera takes her point of view (handbag-cam, a hand at the lens).

ai_production_rules: Lock the product first. Photograph the real CJ sample (SKU CJNSNYNK00343) flat front, flat back, side, stretched, and under black leggings. HOLD all product-frame generation and the brief character model sheet until these 5 photos exist. They're the reference for EVERY AI tool (Nano Banana, Higgsfield reference elements, Kling elements). Product prompt: 'plain black brief exactly as in the reference photos'. Rise, waistband width, leg line and sheen are copied from the photos, not from text. No lace, no logos, no gusset or seams that aren't on the sample. Never prompt from NUMBER_SHEET §13 (it still lists the old lace product).

The only fabric fact is 95% regenerated fibre / 5% spandex (NUMBER_SHEET §1b). Never render the gusset, layers, a cross-section, absorption, liquid or a pour. No backlit liners (no core show-through).

AI renders never demonstrate performance. No 'no line', 'stays put', dry-result or under-leggings-proof claim from a generated frame. After the brief appears, the AI woman never repeats the trigger: no hard laugh, sneeze or jump, and no frame that 'settles' the moment. On-body shots are getting dressed plus one calm everyday action (sit, walk, reach, press play). The only promise is the end-card text.

Crops: side-on, waist-to-knee, or full figure only. No butt- or crotch-centred framing (Meta adult-content risk). On-body prompt: 'getting dressed, sports top on, side view, waist-to-knee crop, pulling black leggings up over black briefs'. Use start and end frames with a 3s interpolation. Fallback when a model refuses or drifts: hands stretching the brief on a bed, then the pull-up framed knee-to-waistband with the top covering the hip.

AI women: 30-45, varied everyday bodies cast to the measured size run (include larger sizes across the set), warm home light, adults only. Never a doctor, nurse, founder or 'customer'. Never a first-person product line ('these held when I sneezed'). The only lines an AI woman may speak are dramatized moment lines ('Stop! I'll pee myself!'). Standing leg-cross pose: 'knees press together, one foot tucked behind the other ankle, slight dip' (crossed knees while standing render as fused legs).

'Dramatization' goes UPPER-LEFT, about 16% down the frame, inside the 4:5 centre crop: cream Hanken Grotesk at least 4% of frame height, 80% opacity. It stays on screen the whole time an AI woman is shown in the moment (laughing hard, sneezing, pressing her knees together, the jumping-jacks cue): V1-b, V3-a/b/c, S4-b. A woman only wearing or handling the product needs no label, but captions never imply she's a real tester. On statics the tag sits inside the image above any footer, and the 9:16 Stories export keeps it above the bottom 35%.

Safe zones: every text block and label sits inside the 4:5 centre crop and above the bottom 35% of a 9:16 frame (roughly 15-60% of frame height). Reels UI covers the bottom 35%, and feed shows 9:16 cropped to 4:5.

AI disclosure: check in Ads Manager whether an AI-disclosure option exists for this ad type and use it if it does. Either way, keep the C2PA/IPTC metadata from Veo, Nano Banana or Higgsfield (don't strip it on export or re-encode) so Meta can apply 'AI info'. Add one caption line under the body copy: 'Made with AI. Product images based on the real brief.' Keep the AI-image line in the landing footer (part of L0-L3).

Talking characters (V2): Pixar-style, built from model sheets. The brief character is built from the sample photos, with its face on the upper front near the waistband, never the crotch. The liner is clean, white and unbranded, sheepish not villainous. Liners and pads anywhere in the set are never stained, yellowed or branded.

V2 voice pipeline. Path A (default): Veo 3 image-to-video per line from the locked model-sheet frame, with the dialogue in the prompt. Then ElevenLabs Voice Changer (speech-to-speech) into the two saved character voices (Brief = warm, dry, mid-30s; Liner = higher, fussy, fast), so voices match across shots and lip timing is kept. Path B: ElevenLabs lines first, then a lip-sync model built for cartoon faces (e.g. Hedra Character-3), with Veo/Kling for non-speaking reactions. Test one 8s line both ways before building the 35s.

Character consistency: one character reference per woman and per object (Higgsfield Soul ID / Kling elements), reused across every shot. Generate in 3-8s shots and cut on reactions. No more than 1 cut in the first 1.2s of any hook. Regenerate any shot with lip-sync drift, extra or fused fingers or legs, garment morphing (into a boyshort or thong) or colour/sheen drift. Don't fix them in the edit.

Props and sets: no real or lookalike trademarks (Always, Carefree, Poise, car badges, real workout programs or TV logos). Liners are shown in pastel unbranded wrappers or clean and half-peeled, never loose and unwrapped on a floor or in a bin (reads as used). For match cuts, generate ONE locked plate and composite the changing props in the edit; vary the light with a grade, never a re-generation.

Audio: no commercial or 'trending' music and no real program audio in any ad. Use Meta Sound Collection or a licensed royalty-free library (Epidemic/Artlist), picked in the current trending style. Any TV or trainer voice is generated in ElevenLabs. One impersonal ElevenLabs brand narrator (a warm, wry woman in her 30s, accent matched to the launch market). Record VO first and cut to it.

Tools: Nano Banana for start frames and statics. Veo 3 for talking characters (native lip-sync, then Voice Changer). Kling 2.x for body motion and start/end-frame interpolation (the leggings pull-up). Higgsfield as the hub for references. ElevenLabs for the narrator, character voices and Voice Changer.

All on-screen text is added in the edit (CapCut/Premiere/Canva), never generated. Hook and moment lines use Hanken Grotesk ExtraBold, upright (matching the live hero's bold sans). Fraunces is for end-card brand lines and the S4-c title. Colours: Plum Ink #231017 / Claret #A33154 / Warm Cream #F5EDE6 / Blush #E7CFC9. Every hero line is copied character for character from the frozen landing. If the hero is restyled at the freeze, re-match the type.
